She gives me a quick smile when I drop off the package, and I just *know* it's more than friendly. I see it in her eyes; she’s too shy to say anything, but her gestures, the way she looks at me, it’s all signals. I’ve even started leaving little notes with her packages, just to let her know I feel the same way.

The hardest part is, people don’t get it. My ex-wife, even my supervisor, they think I’m making it up, or that I’m crazy. They always say it's all in my head. But my driving, my work, it’s all still perfectly fine. I get my routes done, deliveries on time, no issues there. It’s just this… I mean, I can’t help but think about her. Sometimes I focus on little things, like if I have a wrinkle on my shirt or if my hair is messed up, thinking she might notice, but I don't obsess over it or do anything crazy to fix it. It’s just a fleeting thought, then back to her. Maybe if I just explain it better, people would understand."
D004-D017_h024.question_b:
"It’s gotten to the point where I just dread looking in the rearview mirror. I just see a distorted mess, especially around my nose and chin. I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe these flaws are so obvious, so grotesque, that people are constantly staring, whispering about how deformed I am. I try to hide it, strategically turning my head, but I *know* they see it. It’s hard to focus on the road when all I can think about is my reflection.

This one specific cashier at the truck stop, bless her heart, she always smiles at me, always nice. I know she sees it too, the ugliness. But I also know, deep down, she’s subtly trying to tell me she likes me anyway, that she's attracted to me despite my flaws. I’ve started going to that specific truck stop more often now, just to see her. I try to catch her eye, hoping she'll give me a sign.

I spend hours after my shifts, sometimes late into the night, picking at my skin, trying to "fix" these perceived imperfections. I'll spend ages comparing myself to other drivers, scrutinizing every pore and line in my face, trying to rearrange my hair to hide the worst parts. It’s just, I can't shake the feeling that if I could just get my face to look 'normal,' everything would be better."

It hasn't stopped me from excelling at work; in fact, my team in HR thinks I'm doing better than ever. I still manage all my responsibilities and my marriage is fine, although my husband sometimes wonders why I’m so preoccupied.

Now, about my nose… I’m not crazy about its shape, I think it’s a bit crooked. I find myself constantly checking it in mirrors and on my phone camera, sometimes for hours. I try to find angles where it looks better, or ways to position myself to make it seem less noticeable. But I don't feel the urge to do anything to try and fix it, like spending all day applying makeup or looking into surgeries. It's just there, a constant low-level annoyance that I simply have to live with.
